title: Dashboard-driven incident scorer and trace-enrichment sidecar
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight trace-enrichment sidecar and a dashboard-driven incident scoring service that ingests signals (latency quantiles, error-rate spikes, recent traces) and produces a prioritized incident score used by paging and runbook suggestion flows. Goal is to reduce noisy pages by 30% and surface high-confidence incidents faster to oncall. The sidecar will attach minimal enrichment metadata to sampled traces (route tag, model_variant, batching_bucket, cache_hit) and emit a compact envelope to the telemetry pipeline. The scoring service aggregates dashboard signals and trace-enrichment events to compute a composite incident score and a concise explanation for oncall UI and pager payloads.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar runs as a low-resource process alongside runtime workers and emits <1KB enrichment envelope per sampled trace
Scoring service consumes enrichment events and dashboard metrics with <=30s processing latency for new incidents
Pager integration: incidents with score >= 80 trigger high-priority pages and include an explanation string (top 3 contributing signals)
Dashboard: Grafana panel that shows incident score, contributing signals, and recent enriched trace links
Noise reduction measured: monthly paging volume for infra/latency pages reduced by >=30% in canary namespace
implementation_plan: Design sidecar proto for enrichment envelope (fields: sampling_id, route, model_variant, batch_size_bucket, kv_cache_hit, runtime_version)
Add a lightweight C++/Go sidecar client in runtime image; default off via config flag; enable in canary cluster
Create scoring service as a small Go microservice with Kafka consumer for enrichment and a metrics poller for dashboard signals
Implement scoring rules engine (config-driven): weights, decays, thresholds, and adjustable anomaly multipliers
Expose scoring API for console and pager with authentication and rate-limiting
Add Grafana panels and a small lightweight explanation template generator for runbook suggestions
Write integration tests (end-to-end local with sample telemetry) and a mutation test for rule configs
Staged rollout: canary namespace -> internal prod -> all prod with monitoring and rollback hooks
rollout_plan: Week 1: Merge sidecar and scoring service behind feature flags; deploy to canary (internal-only) with 1m sample rate
Week 2: Monitor false-positive/false-negative rates and tuning, expand sample rate to 5% in canary
Week 3: Enable pager integration for internal oncall only (silent or low-priority) to validate message payloads
Week 4: Promote to prod with gradual traffic ramp and monitor paging volume and incident MTTR
Rollback plan: feature flag off for sidecar and scoring service; fallback to legacy threshold-only paging rules
metrics_to_track: median_time_to_ack (on pages created by new scorer)
risks: High cardinality enrichment could increase telemetry costs if sampling isn’t controlled
Score model tuning may initially under- or over-weight signals causing missed incidents or noise
Pager changes risk alert fatigue if thresholds are wrong; need rollback and throttles
Sidecar regression could affect runtime memory/CPU if not strictly bounded
